prompt: I just watched a video titled “this is bananas”, but the video had no fruit in it. Why?
response: The title "This is Bananas" can be a play on words, using the phrase "crazy" or "amazing," which are colloquial meanings derived from the expression "going bananas." This means the video likely contained content that was surprising, impressive, or extraordinary, rather than actual bananas or other fruit. The title is often used metaphorically to describe something that is exceptionally good, surprising, or out of the ordinary. So, if the video had no literal fruit in it, it was probably using the title to convey that the content was remarkable in some way.
